Design Reference Wiki

The browsable system-design pages for Threadbearer. This hub and the nav on every page are generated from public/wiki-manifest.json by scripts/generate-design-wiki.ts on every build.

Manual

A Run, Start to Finish

The shape of a whole run — remembrance and your two domains, the opening spine and The First, the middle game, how either clock ends the run, and what the World-Soul carries into the next.

Reaches, Spheres & Quintessence

The two axes of every divine act — Eight Reaches (what you do) and Twelve Spheres (what fuels it), orthogonal by design — plus each Reach's virtue/vice moral axis, the Domain Capability word-ladder, and Quintessence as narrative centrality (not a ninth Reach).

The Three-Beat Turn

How a turn works — the world waits until you advance it; each turn runs scan → curated moment → aftermath in a load-bearing order; time in ticks (two hours, twelve per day); and encounters as rationed chapters, not per-tick rolls.

Divine Actions & Prerequisites

The five verbs every divine act reduces to (Create/Find/Change/Destroy/Control), why some action cards never appear (Reach outside your two domains — permanent; sphere misalignment; too little capability), the Generalized Action Targeting cascade, and the two reach signatures you acquire as story moments.

Threads, the Court & The First

The thread as a two-way bond — your investment depth (the five influence tiers) versus the mortal's awareness (unaware → intuition → faith → communion); the four court positions; The First's doom-clock-scheduled hero's journey; familiarity as player-side progressive disclosure; and why holding a thread deeply costs upkeep and makes you louder to rivals.

Essence, Control & Sustained Power

Divine fuel is per-Sphere and tight on purpose — where essence comes from (a baseline flow, worshippers, places of power, an Aspect's conduit) and how it splits along your alignment (0.35/0.25/0.40); Control as sustained commitment (upkeep, the slot cap, the three ways a working lapses); the usurp/destroy contestation trade where age is the defence; and the long strategic works that erode when neglected.

Encounters & Aftermath

The encounter as a framed chapter, not a die roll — the two shapes (branching and recurring) that share one UnifiedActionTemplate format; hex-granular awareness (see the hex, see everything on it); the single sigmoid→d100 resolution curve for peasants and gods, with doubles-based crits; aftermath as the mortal's trajectory shift; failure as plot; and the four encounter design rules. Player-voice layer over the deep encounters-agents-reference page.

Doom, the Mandate & Omens

The two clocks that pressure every run from opposite directions — the Doom Clock (seven archetypes, five Whispers→Culmination stages, escalations as world events) counting down to an Unmaking that always lands, and the Victory Mandate (three stages, your declared win-state) counting up; the one-pool-two-clocks tension made concrete by mandate checkpoints that bank counter-omens or owe doom severity; and omens as the pressure made visible.

Reading the Interface

A guided tour of the game screen — the one-viewport, no-scroll contract; the always-on frame (essence, the two clocks, omens, attention, identity, rivals); the drill-in from hex to location to sublocation; the panels (threads, chronicle, narrative feed); the Action Drawer; the encounter surfaces and the deeper sheets; and a cross-reference from every other Manual page to the surface where its system shows its face. Source spine is the IA manifest (63 surfaces).

The Mortals

The mortals who fill the world and pursue their own goals — how a free mortal chooses (a Maslow-inspired, survival-first, values-driven seeded selection, not a literal six-tier ladder); the nine virtue↔flaw value pairs (eight Reach-bound plus courage/prudence) and the slow moral drift a god can bend; ambitions in seven shapes; growth through doing and the five ways a mentorship ends; and the lifecycle from birth to death and the ambient→notable→spotlight graduation that turns a background face into a named individual.

Traits & Marks

The trait layer — a named piece of identity that does nothing on its own and everything when something reads it. Definitions as graph nodes and assignments as has_trait edges; the ten categories as lifecycle contracts (acquisition, removal, trigger) rather than labels, with destiny reserved and empty; the four ref forms that all resolve through one predicate; the four hook shapes a trait reacts through, each naming its trait to the player; visible-once-known; and the capped separation between steering what a mortal reaches for and how well they do it.

Factions, Cultures & Secrets

The social fabric over the mortals — factions as bodies with their own designs (per-faction reputation ladders, autonomous ambitions and actions, mortal succession, schism, and the chosen-faction anointing); cultures as gravity wells you are born inside of (venerated Spheres, generated names and mores, cultural gravity and the four tensions); and the unseen currency of secrets and favors that tilt a social encounter before a word is spoken.

The World: Hexes, Terrain & Sight

The world as a grid of hexes you can shape — the three nested tiers of place (hex → location → sublocation, one rung at a time); terrain and how divine influence, corruption, and per-location magical saturation remake it; and the two hex-distance sight systems, the god's fog of war (unexplored → visible → remembered) and each mortal's own encounter awareness. Load-bearing: hexes are flat array state, not graph nodes.

Settlements, Prosperity & Trade

How settlements rise and fall on their own — the four tiers (hamlet → town → city, with capital fixed) and the sustained-prosperity thresholds that promote or demote them; prosperity as an equilibrium value drifting toward conditions and unrest as a settlement's instability; trade routes that decay when un-travelled; and terrain-seeded resources plus rare anomalies that set a place's ceiling. Honest scope: the economy is texture serving story, not a trading sim.

Livelihoods & the Resource Web

The activated resource economy (Phase 1) — how every place's Livelihood reads in prose from its resource stock tiers (scarce/adequate/surplus), when a staple crosses into Famine or Glut, how supply-vs-demand balance nudges prosperity, how a bonded mortal's home turning hungry pulls a livelihood thread tug, and the resource-class table that leans each good toward a Sphere. Companion to the settlements page; honest scope: P1 activates the layer, trade cargo and divine verbs come later.

Armies, Battles & Lairs

War as a story generator, not a wargame — armies that factions raise for conquest or revenge (three sizes, terrain-punished marches, Quintessence-cohesion attrition and its four threshold encounters); field battles that resolve as a momentum struggle over several turns, tilted by thread-gated spotlights and leaving destruction, captured commanders, and refugees in their wake; sieges as an accelerating battle subtype where walls favour the defender and starvation the attacker; and monster lairs that escalate minor → major (named elite) → legendary (monster faction), poison the land, and reinfest if cleared ground is left untended.

Stealth, Detection & Rival Gods

The two audiences that watch every divine act — mortals whose awareness of you slowly grows, and rival gods who scan the regions for a rising power. How region-level detection pressure climbs with your louder acts and fades when you go quiet (crossing the top seeds a rival strike); the generated rivals (never a fixed pantheon) with their four temperaments and four-phase schemes you can counter; and the hidden marks and ageing intelligence that wait beneath the surface. Honest scope: the finer per-mortal suspicion ladder is designed but dormant; region pressure is what ships.

Attention, the Digest & the Chronicle

How one god watches a whole world without keeping up with all of it — the renewing attention pool (scarce by design, cheaper to attend the mortals closest to you); the curator that sifts the threads and surfaces the few that matter as tugs, promoting genuine turning points to spotlighted story beats on a cooldown; the digest that keeps everything you looked away from, read back through Read the Threads or composed per thread as a story-so-far; and the three-tier prose engine (Routine/Notable/Chronicle) that turns every event into a moment, taught through interactive prose keywords rather than numbers. Honest scope: the digest is appended every tick but its per-tick prune is dormant, so reads self-limit by lookback window.

Twilight, Echoes & the World-Soul

How a run ends and becomes an ingredient of the next — the Unmaking that begins when the Doom clock expires (a twilight you witness, not fight); the harvest that preserves the age's most significant Legacy (mortals), Monument (places), and Relic (artifacts) echoes, scaled by whether the age closed triumphant, somber, or bittersweet; the World-Soul that carries those echoes across cycles as they degrade and binds each run into a chronicle volume; and the next world as a response, not a sequel. Highest-DESIGN-density page: weakened twilight play, divine-echo selection, echoes seeding the next world, a re-drawn cosmos, and the whole Fundament/Resonance ledger are designed but not yet wired — flagged throughout.

The Nudge Card Library

Iterate the repertoire here before content is authored against it.

To document next

Companies & the Travelling Band

The mortal company as a first-class body: how a band forms out of mortals standing together, how cohesion holds it or frays it, how it moves, parts ways, and reunites, and what dissolves it. Today the wiki documents companies only where they touch something else — faction-raised NPC bands on the Factions page, and which encounters a company may take on the Encounters page — so the lifecycle itself (formation, cohesion, movement, parting, reunion, seeking, fray, dissolution) has no page of its own.
